about.title: Health care built around staying strong, not just getting better
body: Sakthi Health Clinic was started with a simple belief: most people only see a doctor once something is already wrong. We wanted to build a clinic that Kolapakkam residents would visit for their everyday energy, fatigue, and wellness concerns too — not just when they're sick.

'Sakthi' means strength and vitality in Tamil, and that's the lens we bring to general medicine — helping you understand what's behind low energy, recurring tiredness, or that nagging feeling that something's off, alongside treating the illnesses that bring most patients through our door.
Whether it's a fever, a full body checkup, or a chronic condition that needs ongoing management, our approach stays the same: listen carefully, explain clearly, and treat the whole person.

blogPosts.title: Why 'Just Being Tired' Is Worth a Doctor's Visit
blogPosts.excerpt: Persistent fatigue is one of the most dismissed symptoms in general medicine — and one of the most useful ones to actually investigate.
blogPosts.author: Dr. Vikram Sundaram
content: Almost every week, a patient tells us some version of the same thing: 'I'm probably just tired, I'm not really sick.' And almost every week, that turns out to be worth a closer look.

Persistent fatigue can come from vitamin D or B12 deficiency, low iron, thyroid imbalances, poor sleep quality, or early-stage chronic conditions like diabetes — all of which are straightforward to test for and, in most cases, straightforward to treat.

The reason fatigue gets dismissed so often is that it doesn't feel urgent the way a fever or an injury does. But low energy that persists for weeks, not days, is your body telling you something worth listening to.

'Sakthi' means strength — and real strength isn't about pushing through exhaustion, it's about understanding what's causing it. A simple consultation and a basic panel of blood tests can often explain months of unexplained tiredness.
If you've been telling yourself you're 'just tired' for more than a few weeks, that's exactly the kind of thing worth bringing to a general physician rather than waiting out.
